candidates.title: Taming the Chaos: Coordinated Autoscaling for Heterogeneous and Disaggregated LLM Inference
candidates.reason: Production-scale coordinated autoscaling for heterogeneous prefill/decode-disaggregated LLM serving. The primary-source abstract reports deployment on tens of thousands of GPUs, topology-aware scheduling, joint prefill/decode scaling, a 26.6 percentage-point utilization gain, and large GPU-hour savings while preserving SLOs. This is strong systems evidence and a meaningful omission if not already represented.

candidates.title: StreamServe: Adaptive Speculative Flows for Low-Latency Disaggregated LLM Serving
candidates.reason: Combines disaggregated prefill/decode serving with adaptive speculative execution and metric-aware routing. The primary-source abstract reports evaluation on four A800 GPUs and large latency reductions versus tensor-parallel vLLM, making it a relevant candidate for the scheduling/disaggregation lineage despite the relatively small evaluation setup.
